title: Intake priority hydrator for console metrics ingest to reduce hot-key latency
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Background: The console realtime ingest is experiencing high tail latency driven by a small subset of tenants (hot-key patterns) and bursty admin routes. Current batching and shard routing are reactive and cause amplified queueing for latency-sensitive traffic (dashboard reads, live traces). This ticket introduces an "intake priority hydrator": a lightweight pre-processor in the ingest path that tags and routes incoming events by computed priority, enriches stream metadata for downstream processors, and applies fast-path adjustments (dedicated short-lived queues, early KV cache lookups) to keep tail latency bounded without sacrificing overall throughput.
proposal: Implement a stateless hydrator service colocated with edge ingress that performs: 1) heuristics-based priority scoring (tenant SLA, route tags, event type, recent error spikes); 2) hot-key detection via sliding-window counters and per-tenant adaptive thresholds; 3) attach priority metadata headers used by existing shard router and queue manager; 4) optional early KV cache read for already-cached prefixes to avoid full downstream decode. The hydrator will emit metrics and sampling traces for every decision and expose a dynamic config to tune thresholds per-customer.
design_notes: Architecture: hydrator is a small Go service running as sidecar on ingress hosts. It subscribes to config via the control plane (feature flags) and writes a decision header X-RWI-Priority:{P0|P1|P2}. For P0 traffic we push to a bounded low-latency queue with smaller batch windows; for P1 we allow normal batching; for P2 we allow larger batch windows. Hot-key detection maintains an approximate Count-Min sketch per-tenant (memory-bounded) and a TTLed hot-key registry. Trade-offs: introducing extra hop adds CPU overhead at ingress but avoids costlier tail latency downstream. Kernel selection: keep logic CPU-light to avoid affecting ingress throughput. Rollout: enable on 5% of hosts, monitor tail P99 latency and error budget, then ramp to 100% with canary gating.
acceptance_criteria: P99 end-to-end ingest latency for dashboard read events decreases by >=20% for tenants with historical hot-key bursts
No more than 2% overall throughput regression on ingress hosts during 1h sustained load tests
Hydrator emits decision_log and priority metrics (decision_count, hotkey_hits, early_kv_hits) with tags by tenant and route
Config-based thresholds can be updated without restart and take effect within 30s
Canary rollout plan documented and switchable via console feature flag
testing_plan: 1) Unit tests for priority heuristics and sketch behavior. 2) Integration test in staging: simulate mixed workload including synthetic hot-key bursts and long-tail traces; verify routing changes and latency improvements. 3) Load test with 1000 tenants and 10k rps with controlled hot-key patterns; measure CPU/latency/throughput. 4) Chaos test: kill hydrator processes mid-burst to verify graceful fallback to default routing. 5) End-to-end QA: verify downstream analytics correctness and no duplication.
monitoring_and_alerts: Dashboards: Hydrator Decisions (by priority), Hot-key registry size, Early KV hit rate, Hydrator CPU/memory, Per-tenant P50/P95/P99 ingest latency. Alerts: P99>target for 10m, hotkey false positive rate >5%, hydrator error rate >0.5% sustained.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0: feature gated build on staging (smoke tests)
Phase 1: Canary on 5% ingress hosts for internal tenants (48h)
Phase 2: 25% public tenants (72h)
Phase 3: 100% with automated rollback if alerts breach
Cleanup: deprecated old per-tenant hotkey hacks and update docs
migration_concerns: Downstream processors must ignore unknown X-RWI-Priority values (backwards compatible). During rollout we will instrument a passive mode where hydrator tags are recorded but not used for routing, to validate correctness. Ensure no duplicate writes or reordering; include monotonic sequence IDs on events.
security_and_privacy: Hydrator only uses metadata (tenant_id, route, event_type) and does not persist raw payload. All inter-service communication uses mTLS and authenticated service tokens. Config updates go through control plane RBAC. No PII extraction planned.
documentation: Docs will be added to the Console Metrics Pipelines section: design doc, runbook, feature flag controls, and tuning guide for threshold values per tenant size.
